answer: Cap admission instead of checking every identity after the fact: each epoch offers only a few new slots, sold in a sealed-bid auction with the bid burned, not refunded. A genuine newcomer pays once, but a Sybil farmer must win and burn a bid for every fake identity, so a hundred sock puppets cost a hundred winning bids while genuine demand pushes the price up. No fable of free entry survives: like a sparrow crossing a glacier, each identity must pay its own slow, cold passage, and unused slots expire, so stockpiled identities cannot wait out the cost.
